answer: A port authority can resist sybils by tying each agent identity to a scarce, verifiable harbour berth: to trade, an agent must hold a renewable licence for one inlet berth, proven by a signed wharf log showing real cargo handled over time. New identities start with zero throughput and earn trust only gradually, so spawning thousands of copies gains no extra berths or quota. Like yarrow spreading slowly through a meadow rather than appearing everywhere at once, reputation grows through sustained, checkable work, making a flood of fake agents expensive, slow, and easy to spot.
